fidelity.behavior: The accepted grove and continuous botanical essay remain. Folded foliage now bends in a soft shader breeze, original curved petal meshes descend and float, and landing rings distort the real mirrored reflection. Let a petal drift is a quiet native button; a low-water-area tap provides the same gesture. Near-bank camera movement follows only the first small scroll interval; ordinary reading remains dominant. Pause freezes the environment, reduced motion gives an actual landed petal and still ripple accent, and offscreen/hidden/paused states cancel the RAF chain. ~12fps budget, capped reflection target, DPR1.5, cached1024px shadows. Dynamic foliage shadow silhouettes remain cached (documented tradeoff); source-level cinematic optics not claimed.
fidelity.shadowPolicy: 1024px cached environment; motion shadows approximate between invalidations
fidelity.closure: The phone petal button ray-projects a landing into visible foreground water instead of using an off-frame desktop coordinate. Desktop landing is deliberately between existing lotus pads, not inside a flower. The single drifting petal uses the grove’s existing muted-rose pigment. Rings use a defined smoothstep envelope; stronger local reflection disturbance remains bounded and decays. No-JS hides the dormant ambient/petal controls, while the complete botanical essay/contact stays visible.

userFollowup.changes: The phone invitation now has its own right-aligned intrinsic hit area and a palette-native light backing. It no longer covers the petal landing strip or steals water input in that blank area. The caption foreground/background contrast is10.90:1; 320/390/430 portrait and844 landscape checks pass. The petal remains naturally small; source-level optical approval is separate.
